role_context.text: Intellihub is a major Australian energy technology company providing smart-metering and related energy solutions across Australia and New Zealand. In 2024, Intellihub supported 40+ electricity retailers; by 2026 it had become the #1 smart-meter provider in ANZ, delivering 99.5% of meter data reliably.

At Intellihub, I worked across two platforms: IWS (Intellihub Web Services), a Python-based platform used by the operations team for service order management, reporting, and user access management, SmartCore, a new TypeScript/Playwright test automation framework for a new system built on Microsoft Azure and D365 designed to replace IWS
At Intellihub, SmartCore was a new system built on Microsoft Azure and D365 using TypeScript, designed to replace IWS. I tested it using Playwright/TypeScipt/Playwright-BDD.
At Intellihub, I reported to the Test Automation Lead and worked alongside two offshore automation engineers.
My work spans test automation and AI-assisted development. I also run regular knowledge sharing sessions to help the team get practical value from AI tools, not just access to them.
At Intellihub, I also contributed to IMDM, a Java-based system, working across three frameworks in total.

achievements.text: At Intellihub, built the first version of BDD scenarios running in the daily CI pipeline. Before this, BDD scenarios only ran on demand. Now they run daily, giving the team constant feedback.

At Intellihub, owned and optimized CI/CD pipelines across IWS/Jenkins/Python and Azure Pipelines/TypeScript/Playwright-BDD,  reducing manual work for the team. For example, a script that audits Jenkins for stale git branches taking up disk space, and email notifications that flag service health issues in production and test environments.

At Intellihub, created .github/copilot-instructions.md (Agents.md) files in the IWS and SmartCore repos, giving AI agents a repo map and project context at session start, unified set of agent rules used by everyone in a team.

(Intellihub) Took ownership of technical debt. Highlighted existing multiple hardcoded waits, in one of the PRs, replaced them with robust implicit waits and applied Playwright best practices tests to improve test reliability.
(Intellihub) Caught issues early through PR reviews and task coordination, preventing defects from reaching production. Developed and used advanced agent skills for this.
(Intellihub) Supported the dev team during weekend production rollouts, including preparing, stopping, and restarting Jenkins CI jobs.
(Intellihub) Over the 8 months, I ran 8 knowledge sharing sessions on AI-assisted development, testing, and automation.
(Intellihub), Created blog posts from session transcripts and shared them with the team.
Ran daily pipeline checks, built BDD scenarios from existing steps, and created shareable test reports for stakeholders.

At Figtree Systems, built the first UI test automation framework from scratch and deployed a Playwright UI suite with 50+ automated scenarios, leading the work. It saved 4-6 hours of manual work per regression run.
At Figtree Systems, made test coverage visible with a Jira dashboard. Manual test coverage grew from 20-30% to 50-70% in under 4 months.

At WithYouWithMe, tested the migration of courses from AWS to Azure storage. Prioritized the top 10 most popular courses from usage data, built an Excel script tool that checked file availability, and reported multiple migrated files missing or inaccessible.

ai_enablement.text: Created 5 GitHub Copilot Skills for shared team use, covering IWS domain knowledge, task creation, and AI skill best practices. 2 to 3 team members confirmed using them in daily work.
Built 15 or more additional AI skills and prompts for my own AI-assisted development workflow.

Developed an AI-powered PR review agent: a skill package with scripts, templates, and references. It reduces token usage, produces structured review reports with verdict, summary, and suggestions, and saves an estimated 5 to 10% time per review.
Created Agents.md instructions for both IWS and SmartCore frameworks. These load at the start of each AI session and give the assistant the right context and guidance for the project.

Built an AI-powered scheduled workflow (uses small, cheap LLM via Copilot CLI) that automatically analyses execution results of automated regression test suite for testing environment; combines deterministic and LLM steps that save engineers time for initial analysis and produce failure root-cause (defect, test script issue, etc), confidence level of analysis, label failure with domain or component tag, suggests next steps and what team to escalate to, generates concise summary with 1-line verdicts and highlighted grouped test failure. It runs daily against test environment. Instead of going through each test result manually, test engineer gets a quick overview at a glance

Built the AI analysis tool on the team's BDD framework so other engineers and stakeholders can reuse AI-powered steps written in plain language, and edit steps without code changes in the Jira and Zephyr web editor.
Created copilot-instructions.md as reusable guidance for AI collaboration, so team members do not have to set up context from scratch each time.
Shared AI skills, agents, session recordings, and blog posts broadly with the team.

Built scheduled AI-powered reports that analyse test execution results for IWS framework, and give the team a clear view of high-impact failure areas, classified each failure by category (defect, test script issue, environment issue, etc). Two audience-tailored versions (stakeholders, engineers) use progressive disclosure, scoring rules, and consistent language.

Designed the report workflow with agentic engineering concepts: planning, tool use, self-reflection, and specialized agents. Reused an existing domain-knowledge skill and created new skills to make report generation more efficient and accurate.

Designed instructions and rubrics so a small LLM produces structured output: test failures classified as environment, test data, test script, application, or unknown issues, each with a confidence level so readers know how much to trust the label.

Investigated unexpected Copilot analysis results and traced the cause to a Copilot bug: multiline prompts dropped every line except the first. Implemented the workaround recommended in the GitHub Copilot repo.

Solving todays AI enablement challenges. Authored and shared 3 agent skills that help humans to saty in the loop and make it easuer to process AI generated content. 1) Unslop skill; 2) Response techniques skill; 3) conceptual-model skill 4) explaining-code skill. These skills were utilizing latest insdustry best practices and techniques for prompt engineering, agentic engineering, and LLMs. They are designed to be reusable and adaptable for different contexts and tasks. They help to improve the quality, clarity, and relevance of AI-generated content, as well as to enhance human understanding and decision-making.

personal_projects.text: Built a machine-readable NSW curriculum dataset: 1,500+ learning outcomes extracted from 81 NESA syllabus pages, synced monthly by a GitHub Actions job, with a zero-dependency explorer on GitHub Pages. Scoolendar owner mentioned existing pain point - when creating educational events, it is difficult for users to find relevant learning outcomes and codes (as per NSW standard). I researched, discovered there is no official API, found a workaround (fetch from website) and built POC with public dataset https://github.com/MaksimZinovev/curriculum-learning-outcomes-au .It runs automatically and updates data every month plus GitHub pages provide convenient UI to explore, search and filter data

Built groundcrew, a public CI monitoring bot developed as part of volunteer work with Scoolendar. It reads GitHub Actions results, performs AI analysis of regression testing results, and posts plain-language summaries to Telegram: what failed, why, and where to look. It answers follow-up questions in Telegram using CI data and live website inspection. The bot recalls past failures and human corrections, so repeated issues are flagged instead of re-explained. groundcrew - open and check Telegram chat (10-20 sec).  CI or email - open site, login, 2FA, open pipelines (2-5 mins). That saves time every day. It may look like not much but over a year that can turn into 10-20 hours
personal_projects.note: Public repo. Already in CV GitHub Highlights.

personal_projects.text: Built docfence, a Python CLI with no external dependencies that validates markdown spec documents against rules embedded in the document. It catches issues AI assistants introduce: TODOs, broken links, missing sections, and length overruns.

Wrote starlord, an agent skill that compares starred GitHub repos against locked criteria. Scripts gather metadata first, the LLM sees pre-digested facts for 8 to 12 candidates, and a validation script rejects claims without a source. Set of rubrics and weights helps to calibrate, tune the judgement and scoring. Final table format + concise prose explaining strengths and weaknesses of each candidate makes it easy for user to understand comparison in condensed form and make an informed decision

Created television-skill, an agent skill for the television terminal fuzzy finder, compatible with pi, Claude Code, Codex, and any Agent Skills client. It packages the full channel spec, a scaffold script for custom channels, and 7 documented gotchas. Why its worth attention - saves me few minutes every day on frequently performed tasks like launching local dev servers and commands, searching AI agent skills, generating documents using library of AI prompts, e.g. extract learning note from youtube using LLM, generate note from GitHub readme or any web page; it captures the purpose, sample use cases, key details, how it works in concise format, perfect for curated resources in personal wiki or knowledge base

I built ats-search-tool for the hidden job market. The best roles often live only on employer ATS boards like Greenhouse, Lever or Workday, plus government and university systems, and never reach Seek or LinkedIn. What used to be 29 separate Google searches is now one search.

JEV, a small scoring model from TypeSafe, grades each match 0-4 for keyword match, open job, location fit and still live. Each question carries five written criteria, and results return as typed data, not prose. One batched call scores each platform's snippets, and expanding a row re-checks the full posting page. A deterministic gone-check catches dead postings before the model runs.

Does it work? Not a magic pill, but it works. Two days of use graded 1,000+ postings for about five cents and saved roughly 3-8 hours of link-opening. The best catch was a Flybuys automation engineer role missing from LinkedIn. I applied for it.

Good proof of Applied AI Engineer skills. It shows I can turn agentic AI techniques into working code: structured scores from a small cheap model, criteria anchors, batching, deterministic checks. Built for my own job hunt, not as a demo, and I use it every day.

Significance: high. Fresh, public, in daily use, and it has already caught roles the big boards missed.
personal_projects.note: Public repo, published 2026-10-20. Freshest entry, used daily. Same small-model structured-output pattern as ai-009/ai-011, backed by a public repo. Metrics from job-search-lessons-learned.md: 1,000+ requests, ~$0.05 grading cost, 10-30s saved per posting, Flybuys role catch. Featured as a LinkedIn story post with screenshots (not yet on the profile). Time savings restated as aggregate: 10-30s per posting x 1,000+ posts = roughly 3-8 hours over two days (derived, check before use).

personal_projects.text:
I built job-application-workflow, a skill that runs a job application as a gated pipeline. Instead of a cover letter written blind, my applications start with a score. Python grades the ad against my rubric with web search grounding, and I decide to promote the job or drop it, so a bad fit never costs a letter.

The LLM writes prose, Python does every check. Draft one faces mechanical rules, em dashes, cliches, keyword coverage. A fresh-context judge then scores it against a six-dimension rubric. Rewrites become v2 while v1 stays on disk, and a retro distills each run into learned rules for the next one. Every step stops at a checkpoint I approve.

More than thirty jobs have gone through scoring in my real hunt, and three interviews came out of those applications. Good proof of Applied AI Engineer skills. It shows LLM-as-judge, tiered verification, rubric design and human gates working in code. Not a demo. It decides which jobs get my time and drafts the letters I send.

Significance: high. Real usage, thirty scored jobs, three interviews already, and public code.
personal_projects.note: Public repo (Sep 2026). Real usage evidence in wiki notes/2026-job-scoring: numbered scoring runs up to 37, scoring.md on rubric axes (salary, job type, company size, culture, location, roles), rule-checks.json, self-improvements.md retros feeding learned rules. 'More than thirty' derived from folder numbering, confirm. Outcome metric confirmed by user 2026-10-20: 3 interviews from 30+ scored applications.

personal_projects.text:
I've maintained Scoolendar's automated test suite as volunteer QA and automation engineer since August 2025. Scoolendar is an educational events platform aligned to NSW curriculum, and its founder develops solo part-time, so there's no QA role. My suite and its CI runs are the safety net for every release.

Around 100 Playwright tests (UI+API) in 20 spec files run in CircleCI on every change, and they've stayed green for over a year while the product changed underneath them. When views changed, I updated selectors. When tests depended on each other's data, I reworked them to be self-contained, so failures stay isolated. That's 13 months and roughly 175 repository commits.

For me, this was an opportunity to run quality for a real product as a one-person function: design the suite, keep tests independent, keep the net working while the product moves. Good proof of Test Automation and Quality Engineering skills together: Playwright, CI discipline, self-contained test design, long-horizon maintenance. Significance: medium-high. Real product, real users, sustained volunteer ownership.

**Repository:** private (scool-playwright).
